THE BUSINESS QUESTION

Where do delivery performance and profitability vary across orders, shipping modes, and product categories?

An operations analysis spanning 65,752 orders, 20,652 customers, and 50 product categories. This case-study summary is based on the project description in my resume.

FROM RAW DATA TO INSIGHT

What I worked on.

  1. 01

    Examine the order-item dataset

    Analyzed 180,519 order items with Python and Pandas, covering delivery performance, profitability, and sales.

  2. 02

    Compare delivery performance

    Measured late delivery among non-canceled shipments and compared shipping modes to identify performance gaps.

  3. 03

    Evaluate commercial performance

    Assessed order value after discounts, profit margin, loss-making orders, and category-level concentration.

THE FINDINGS

What the data revealed.

Concentration of order value

Top 3 categories
42.08%
Other 47 categories
57.92%

Top-three share from the resume; remaining share calculated as 100% − 42.08%.

Delays affect a majority of shipments

57.31% of non-canceled shipments arrived late, with delays averaging 1.62 days.

Margin hides unprofitable orders

The analysis evaluated 33.05 million in post-discount order value and a 12.00% profit margin, while identifying 13,909 loss-making orders.

Value is concentrated in a few categories

Three of the 50 product categories contributed 42.08% of order value.

FROM FINDING TO NEXT STEP

Where the analysis points.

  • Investigate delivery gaps by shipping mode.
  • Examine the drivers of loss-making orders alongside the overall margin.
  • Review the operational importance of the categories contributing the most order value.

Proposed next steps based on the analysis.

Source & scope

Only the resume summary was supplied for this project. The source does not specify the monetary currency or document an implemented business improvement; no reduction in delays or increase in profit is claimed here.
